source.quote: SMSL's own page for the RAW-DAC1, read 2026-11-27 with curl, « Introduction » bullets: « Using AK4191+AK4499EX to play the full performance of Chips, the distortion is as low as 0.00006%(-124dB); »; « XMOS XU-316, true 32bit USB processing, supports DoP and Native DSD, and PCM reach up to 768kHz and DSD512; »; « USB, Optical and Coaxial support DSD transmission, Coaxial, Optical support DOP64; »; « The latest Bluetooth supports LDAC, APTX/HD, SBC, AAC; »

facts.chip: AKM AK4499EX converter with an AK4191EQ modulator (« Using AK4191+AK4499EX »), XMOS XU-316 on USB.

_the_ceiling_is_the_XMOS_bullet: The rate and DSD ceilings come from the bullet naming the XMOS USB receiver, so they are written on usb only. No other input is given a PCM rate: the page states none.
_optical_has_DoP64_and_no_rate: Optical and coaxial get DoP64 from the maker's own clause and no PCM ceiling, because none is stated: copying 768 kHz onto optical is the error vocabulary/why-the-optical-default-stays-low.json exists to prevent.
_a_split_AKM_pair: AK4191EQ is AKM's separate delta-sigma modulator and AK4499EX the switched-resistor output stage it drives. family akm covers both; what the split means for DSD (whether DSD bypasses the AK4191's modulator) is not stated on the page.
